summary: Kyoto School, Mohist, ubuntu and Sor Juana scholarship expands candidate and interpretive coverage. Selected original arguments by Mill, Hume and Locke add primary-text evidence; they are not treated as reception votes.
next: More philosophy reader communities and non-English intellectual traditions; nonfiction breadth beyond philosophy.

sources.title: Review: Philosophers of Nothingness
sources.publisher: Journal of Buddhist Ethics / Diana L. Pasulka
sources.note: Pasulka praises Heisig’s accessible organization and account of experiential philosophy, distinguishing Kyoto interpretations from Buddhism generally and tracing intercultural exchange.
sources.limits: Taiwan-hosted copy of an English-language review; not an independent Taiwanese critical judgment.

sources.title: The Philosophy of the Mozi: The First Consequentialists
sources.publisher: Notre Dame Philosophical Reviews / Eirik Lang Harris
sources.note: Harris describes Fraser’s rehabilitation of Mohist impartiality and skill-centered epistemology, linking moral standards to motivation and political order.
sources.limits: Modern consequentialist terminology is an interpretation; school text is not a single-author transcript.

sources.title: Recensie: Mogobe Ramose – Ubuntu
sources.note: Hummel criticizes abstraction, repetition and unexplained communal identity in Ramose, explicitly identifying his own European standpoint and unresolved reader questions.
candidates: Ubuntu: stroom van het bestaan als levensfilosofie
sources.location: Opening and three proposed ubuntu features
sources.limits: Critical outsider response; do not generalize its objections to all African philosophy.

sources.title: Ubuntu and the globalisation of Southern African thought and society
sources.note: Van Binsbergen values Ramose’s globalization critique but treats codified ubuntu as a modern reconstruction and warns against confusing normative aspiration with ethnographic description.
sources.limits: Author discloses collegial ties and participant commitments; mirror/PDF same underlying essay.

sources.title: An Initial Sketch of Sor Juana’s Virtue Epistemology
sources.publisher: Journal of the American Philosophical Association
sources.note: Interprets Sor Juana’s Reply through intellectual humility, curiosity and publicly discernible epistemic agency, explaining how these arguments resist gendered restrictions on learning.
candidates: Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz
sources.location: Introduction and statement of four interpretive claims
sources.limits: Virtue-responsibilist classification is the article’s reconstruction; not Sor Juana’s own terminology.

sources.title: On Liberty — selected passages
sources.note: Mill defends discussion through fallibility and grounds liberty in utility, yet explicitly excludes societies he deems unready for free discussion.
sources.location: Chapters I–II: scope, utility and infallibility
sources.limits: Selected passages only; colonial exclusion is recorded alongside the defense, not endorsed.

sources.title: An Enquiry Concerning Human Understanding — selected passages
sources.note: Hume distinguishes repeated conjunction from insight into causal power and explains inferential expectation through habit while retaining ordinary practical reasoning.
sources.limits: Selected passage; a primary argument is not an independent vote for its truth or influence.

sources.title: Second Treatise of Government — selected passages
sources.note: Locke connects appropriation to labor and sufficient resources remaining for others, then distinguishes common land held by compact and enlarged holdings through money.
sources.location: Chapter V, sections 27–36 and money discussion
sources.limits: Selected property argument; its normative and colonial implications require separate critical comparison.
